subject.title: Device identity generation should not depend on browser Secure Context — breaks HTTP reverse-proxy deployments

question: Should OpenClaw allow browser Control UI device identity to be generated and used from non-localhost plain-HTTP pages, and if so under what operator-controlled policy?
rationale: The remaining change is not a narrow bug fix: it would move persistent browser operator identity into a plaintext remote delivery context that current docs and tests intentionally reject.

options.title: Keep Rejection Default
options.body: Keep remote plain-HTTP browser identity rejected and rely on HTTPS, localhost, trusted-proxy, Tailscale, or the existing break-glass bypass plus clearer warnings.

options.title: Add Explicit Opt-In
options.body: Allow the behavior only behind a clearly dangerous operator-selected policy with docs, tests, dependency proof, and upgrade/security wording.

options.title: Allow By Default
options.body: Remove the secure-context gate for all browser Control UI sessions, accepting a broader plaintext-LAN trust model.

recommendation.title: Keep Rejection Default
recommendation.body: Keep remote plain-HTTP browser identity rejected and rely on HTTPS, localhost, trusted-proxy, Tailscale, or the existing break-glass bypass plus clearer warnings.

likelyOwner.reason: The current secure-context boundary and recent UI identity code history route most strongly through this owner trail.
